item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 221728
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Oct 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located several hundred miles south of Acapulco,
Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, a few hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll
late this weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the
system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
725 
WTPZ32 KNHC 222036
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
...VANCE CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...10.0N 101.5W
ABOUT 490 MI...785 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 650 MI...1045 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 10.0 North, longitude 101.5 West.  Vance is
moving toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h) and a slow 
northwestward to north-northwestward motion is expected over the 
next few days. 

Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 65 mph (100 km/h) 
with higher gusts.   Vance is forecast to become a hurricane 
tonight, and it could become a major hurricane by the weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 222037
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026

Satellite imagery shows that Vance continues to become better 
organized and is strengthening.  The storm has numerous convective 
bands, especially over its southern semicircle, and a small 
developing Central Dense Overcast.  Upper-level outflow is becoming 
well defined over all quadrants of the circulation.  The advisory 
intensity is set at 55 kt in agreement with a subjective Dvorak 
classification from TAFB.  This is also close to a blend of the 
various objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS.

The center appears to be moving west-northwestward with a motion 
estimate of 300/4 kt.  Vance is currently south of a mid-level high 
pressure area over western Mexico.  Over the next few days, this 
ridge is forecast to weaken as a trough moves into the southwestern 
United States.  As a result the tropical cyclone should turn toward 
the northwest and north-northwest over the next 72 hours.  Late in 
the forecast period, the trough moves eastward and leaves Vance in 
a region of weak steering currents.  The official forecast track is 
nudged a little east of the previous one and is generally a blend 
of the Google DeepMind ensemble and the NOAA corrected consensus, 
HCCA, solution.

Vance is in an environment that is generally conductive for 
significant intensification during the next couple of days, with low 
vertical wind shear, high oceanic heat content and plenty of 
mid-level moisture.  The NHC intensity forecast remains about the 
same as in previous advisories and near the high end of the model 
guidance suite.  However it should be noted that the track of the 
cyclone could eventually take it over waters that have been cooled 
by the passage of recent tropical cyclones.  This, along with some 
increase in vertical shear later in the forecast period, could 
limit strengthening.  So, there is a fair amount of uncertainty in 
the future intensity of Vance.
